name: Onion Rava Dosa
steps: Whisk semolina, rice flour, plain flour and salt with the measured water into a very thin batter. Add cumin and finely minced ginger; leave it for 20 minutes.
Finely dice onion and green chilli. Stir them into the batter just before cooking, then stir again before each dosa because semolina sinks and onion floats.
Heat a well-seasoned griddle until hot. Splash a ladleful of batter from outside towards the centre, allowing many tiny holes to remain; do not spread it like an ordinary dosa.
Drizzle a little of the measured oil into the holes and around the edges. Cook for 3–4 minutes until crisp and deep golden underneath, loosening the edges carefully.
Fold each dosa and serve at once with prepared coconut chutney. Add a splash of water if the final batter becomes thick; it must flow freely for a lacy crust.
tips: Dice onion very small so pieces adhere to the thin lace instead of tearing it.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
